reference_answer: docker compose config renders the resolved Compose application model after files are merged and interpolation is applied. docker compose config --environment shows the environment values Compose uses for interpolation. The first reveals the resulting model; the second helps explain where interpolation inputs came from.
scoring_focus: Distinguish the resolved model from the environment used to interpolate it.

reference_answer: A named volume is managed by Docker, persists independently of a container and is not tied to a user-selected host path. A bind mount maps a specific host path and makes host files directly visible to the container. A tmpfs mount lives in memory and is removed when the container stops, so it is not persistent.
scoring_focus: Compare persistence, management and host visibility for all three mount types.

reference_answer: First inspect the resolved Compose model with docker compose config and inspect interpolation inputs with docker compose config --environment. Then compare the service environment and env_file definitions, the image ENV defaults and any docker compose run -e override. Finally inspect the environment inside the actual container. Interpret the result using Compose environment precedence: run -e and explicit environment values can override env_file and image ENV, while interpolation determines values inserted into the Compose model.
scoring_focus: Provide an ordered diagnostic procedure and separate interpolation from runtime precedence.

reference_answer: Test an external domain and a Compose service name separately from inside the same container. If service names work, Compose network membership and internal service discovery are functioning. Inspect the Compose network with docker network inspect, then inspect Docker daemon DNS settings and test the configured external resolvers. Correct daemon DNS for external domains without changing working Compose service discovery.
scoring_focus: Give a reproducible sequence that isolates external DNS from internal Compose discovery.

reference_answer: Shell variables, the default .env file or an explicit --env-file provide inputs for Compose interpolation, subject to interpolation precedence. The interpolated value can be written into the service environment in the resolved Compose model. For the one-off container, docker compose run -e has high runtime precedence; explicit service environment values override env_file and image ENV, while image ENV is only a lower-priority default. The exact winner therefore depends on scope: interpolation input and container runtime environment must be evaluated separately.
scoring_focus: Correctly separate interpolation scope from runtime environment precedence and identify the high-priority run override.

reference_answer: The working or project directory affects default .env discovery, Compose file discovery and the default project name. COMPOSE_FILE can select or merge other files, while -p has high precedence for the project name over COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and directory-derived defaults. Make execution deterministic by fixing the Compose files, project directory or --project-directory, env file and project name explicitly, then verify the result with docker compose config and its environment output.
scoring_focus: Connect directory-dependent discovery and project-name precedence to a reproducible execution configuration.

reference_answer: network_mode: host places the API in the host network namespace instead of the normal Compose bridge network. Therefore it is not a normal member of the Compose network that provides service-name DNS for db. A healthy db does not change that missing network path. Remove host networking and attach both services to a shared Compose bridge network, then connect with the db service name and container port; use an explicit host-access mechanism only if host networking is genuinely required.
scoring_focus: Connect namespace choice to missing network membership, failed discovery and the redesign.

reference_answer: The default image files disappear because a mount placed over their directory masks the image contents; the mount does not merge them. The later application data disappears because it was written to the container writable layer rather than persistent storage. Keep immutable defaults at an unmounted image path, initialize or copy them deliberately when needed, and mount a named volume or suitable bind mount only at the application data path that must persist.
scoring_focus: Distinguish mount masking from writable-layer data loss and propose one layout that solves both.

reference_answer: From the host, use docker compose port web PRIVATE_PORT --index 2 to identify the published host port for replica 2. A container should not use that host port for ordinary container-to-container traffic because it should address the service through the Docker network using the service name and container port. For a container in another Compose project, attach both projects to the same pre-created external network and use an unambiguous network alias or service name; exact replica targeting may require a design other than normal service-level discovery.
scoring_focus: Traverse host-side replica lookup, container port semantics and cross-project shared networking.

reference_answer: depends_on with service_healthy waits for the declared healthcheck, but it only helps if that healthcheck tests the correct endpoint. Inside the database container, the check should normally use the database container port, not the published host port. Even after db becomes healthy, web cannot connect by service name unless both services share a Compose network. Correct the healthcheck to test the internal service endpoint, attach both services to a shared network, connect through the db service name and container port, and retain application retry logic for transient failures.
scoring_focus: Explain the complete chain from an invalid readiness signal to a separate network reachability failure.

reference_answer: Compose service names are stable discovery identifiers on a Compose network, while a recreated container can receive a different IP address. Demonstrate this by inspecting the network before and after recreation with docker network inspect and observing the changed container IP while the service name remains the intended endpoint. Clients should resolve the service name again and reconnect after failures rather than cache a container IP.
scoring_focus: Provide both the causal explanation and a concrete observation that verifies it.

reference_answer: An external network is managed outside the current Compose project and Compose expects a network with the exact configured name to exist. Another project may have created a project-prefixed network whose visible name only looks similar. List and inspect networks with docker network inspect, compare the exact name with the Compose external network declaration, then either create the required network with docker network create, set the correct external name, or use a deliberately shared external network in both projects.
scoring_focus: Ground the ownership and naming explanation in verifiable network inspection and a precise repair.
